transcript.content: v1.34.6 regression: ares_fetch_connection rejects connections when consec_failures > 0, causing UDP socket exhaustion under load A regression introduced in v1.34.6 (via #1032) causes c-ares to open a new UDP socket for every DNS query when the DNS server has any consecutive failures, instead of reusing existing connections. Under real-world load this produces a 235x increase in UDP socket usage. ## Versions affected - **v1.34.5**: working correctly (baseline) - **v1.34.6**: broken (regression introduced via #1032) node: 22.22.2-bookworm result: node:22.21.1-bookworm result: Metric | Node 22.21.1 | Node 22.22.2 | Delta -- | -- | -- | -- Peak sockets | 13 (+7) | 1,651 (+1,645) | 235x more sockets Amplification | 4.30x | 4.76x | +11% Packets OUT | 26,866 | 29,744 | +11% Packets IN | 14,388 | 13,490 | -6% (more drops) ## Root cause Commit db67e35 in #1032 added the following guard to `ares_fetch_connection()`: ```c if (conn->server->consec_failures > 0) { return NULL; } The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed, find ares_fetch_connection in src/lib (likely ares_process.c or ares_send.c) and print the function with 40 lines of context, with line numbers, and every caller.
